recognize_zh: 低倍周邊血抹片的紅血球背景中，有一條長約數十個紅血球寬度、呈問號狀彎曲的紫色蟲體，為微絲蟲（microfilaria）。
features: Single elongated worm-like larva, many red cell diameters long, coiled into a question-mark shape
Uniformly purple-staining body with a rounded anterior end and tapering tail
Internal nuclear column, sheath and tail nuclei not resolvable at this low magnification
Background of evenly spread red cells; no white cells prominent in this field
describe_en: Low-power view of a peripheral blood smear shows a single long, coiled, worm-like larva with a rounded anterior end and tapering tail among evenly spread red cells. The organism is consistent with a microfilaria. Sheath, nuclear column and tail nuclei cannot be evaluated at this magnification, so species cannot be determined; high-power or thick-film examination (and timing of collection relative to periodicity) is needed to separate Wuchereria bancrofti, Brugia, Loa loa and Mansonella.

ddx.vs: Trypanosomes are only a few red cells long, with an undulating membrane, flagellum and kinetoplast.
Artifacts are refractile, often in a different focal plane, and lack a stained body with internal nuclei and tapered tail.
Borrelia are thin loosely coiled spirochetes about 1-2 red cells long, much smaller and thinner than a microfilaria.
